text:
maya: Heads up — I'm seeing nondeterministic outputs in the eval harness for the new quantized build (ggml-q4_0 variant). Repro on my laptop and on CI but only ~1/6 runs.

sam: ugh. what flags/settings? top_p/temp? batch size?

maya: Default eval config. Temperature 0.0, top_p 1.0 for the deterministic test. Seeds are explicitly set per-run.

jun: Can you paste the CI failure?

eval-bot: CI deterministic-check #1187: failed on model: redwood-ggml-q4_0-v2, seed=42, worker_pool=8, run=3
  checksum_expected: 7d3f9a2c
  checksum_actual:   2e9b1f44

maya: here's a minimal repro log from local:
  --- begin ---
  RUN: eval_runner --config configs/det_test.json --seed 42 --workers 4
  [worker-0] seed init: 42
  [worker-1] seed init: 42
  [worker-2] seed init: 42
  [worker-3] seed init: 42
  model: loaded quant kernels: q4_0_pack_v2
  step 1: token=\"The\"
  step 2: token=\"quick\"
  step 3: token=\"brown\"  <-- differs from expected
  checksum: 2e9b1f44
  --- end ---

lia: Wait worker logs all say seed init: 42? That smells like per-worker RNG state being derived wrongly (not offset by worker id). Could be re-seeding multiple threads to the same state then doing non-deterministic interleaving.

sam: We used to do: rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + worker_id) but in the new runner we changed to rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) and then hand out substreams via .integers for each request. Maybe something flakey in the substream handout.

jun: There's also the quant kernels' use of curand-like device RNG for fused ops in q4 kernels — if they consume entropy differently across batch sizes that could change alignment. Any kernel-change commits recently?

maya: Yes, commit 0a3b changed pack kernel to use continuous batching and a simplified entropy call for top-k/top-p pruning. I'll bisect.

eval-bot: telemetry: observed non-deterministic token positions mostly around token indices 2-6 and when sequence length crosses a multiple of 64.

lia: multiple-of-64 boundary — smells like KV cache chunking or kernel vectorization remainders. If a worker processes partial batch sizes differently, RNG consumption order can shift.

sam: Proposal: implement a deterministic-run mode that gates any kernel-level nondeterminism. Two parts: 1) central RNG manager that hands deterministic per-request sequences (pre-sliced per-worker) 2) kernel-side flag to use CPU fallback RNG or deterministic path when enabled.

jun: Easy to say; harder to land. Alternative quick fix: in CI add a "determinism smoke" step that runs 10 identical seeds and fails if any mismatch. That will catch further regressions.

maya: I already added a flaky CI job that tries 8 repeats and looks for checksum stability. It caught this one. But we need root cause.

lia: Can you run with --trace-rng-order which logs every RNG consume with (worker_id, op_id, seq_num)? We have lightweight hooks in the runtime.

maya: Ran that locally. snippet:
  [rng-trace] (w0,opA) idx=0
  [rng-trace] (w1,opA) idx=0
  [rng-trace] (w0,opB) idx=1
  [rng-trace] (w2,opA) idx=0
  [rng-trace] (w1,opB) idx=1
  ...
  but in failing runs I see an op order flip: (w2,opA) happening before (w0,opB) causing downstream tokens to diverge.

sam: That confirms interleaving. If any kernel does asynchronous device-side RNG consumption that is outside the traced ops, it'll shift indexes.

jun: Another angle: tokenizer differences. Did you pin tokenizer version and BPE merges?

maya: pinned. Also run with deterministic tokenization check — same tokens up to diff point.

lia: Step plan:
  - maya to bisect 0a3b diff to isolate kernel changes
  - sam to add central RNG manager PR that can be toggled by env (REPRO_DETERMINISTIC=1)
  - jun to add kernel-mode flag for deterministic fallback where q4 kernels avoid async device RNG
  - lia to add a CI-wide determinism harness (10 repeats, logs on mismatch) and dashboard metric (determinism_rate)

sam: For the central RNG manager: we should snapshot per-worker starting cursor before each eval run and restore on resume. That avoids checksum drift on resume after checkpoint. Example snippet:
  // pseudo
  cursor = seed * 100000 + run_id
  per_worker_cursor = cursor + worker_id * 1000
  rng = PCG64(per_worker_cursor)

maya: Good. Also found weirdness: when runner resumes from partial-run checkpoints, we weren't serializing the RNG cursor for quantized kernels — only for CPU RNG. So a resumed run can produce different device RNG consumption.

jun: That explains the CI resume flakes. We should include kernel RNG cursor in checkpoint metadata.

deploy-bot: Deploy note: rolling out the kernel patch to staging at 2024-05-21T11:18Z (patch: q4_0_pack_v2 -> q4_0_pack_v2-deterministic)

maya: After the staging kernel patch, reran 20 repeats locally — all stable so far. We'll monitor CI.

lia: Long-term we want: (1) deterministic mode for full-stack reproducibility, (2) telemetry to surface token-index hotspots where nondet appears, (3) automatic bisect CI job that can narrow commit ranges on failure.

sam: I'll open PR for central RNG manager with toggle and tests. Add unit test that runs 5 seeds across 4 workers and asserts identical checksums.

maya: Thanks. One more: let's add an eval-harness flag --require-determinism that CI can flip for release checks.

jun: Also log: include kernel version id and compile flags in checksum metadata so any kernel variant change will reflect in failure triage.

maya: Agreed. I'll update the harness to include kernel hashes.

eval-bot: Note: scheduling the determinism smoke job on every merge to main (low-priority) and nightly higher repetition.

lia: ok team, triage ticket created: ENG-ML-3257 (determinism: sampler/kernel RNG drift). Assigning to sam/maya/jun.

maya: I'll post back with bisection result. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam: thx :coffee:
